body: ### Problem After commit b44c2bdd16, Nvim becomes extremely slow or appears to hang when opening a Python file that contains repeated consecutive f-string literals like the repro below, with Tree-sitter enabled. With 7 repeated f-string lines, Nvim hangs for about 5 seconds. With 8 repeated f-string lines, Nvim hangs for more than 1 minute. ### Steps to reproduce Create `repro.py`: ```python a.a( f"{a}" f"{a}" f"{a}" f"{a}" f"{a}" f"{a}" f"{a}" ) ```` #### If `nvim-treesitter` and the Python parser are already installed Open the file normally with Tree-sitter enabled: ```sh nvim repro.py ``` The slowdown happens while opening the file. #### If `nvim-treesitter` is not installed For a clean repro, clone `nvim-treesitter` into a temporary directory: ```sh git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter /tmp/nvim-treesitter ``` Install the Python parser: ```sh nvim --clean \ +'set rtp^=/tmp/nvim-treesitter' \ +'runtime plugin/nvim-treesitter.lua' \ +'TSInstall python' ``` Wait until `:TSInstall python` finishes, then quit Nvim. Create `repro.vim`: ```vim set runtimepath^=/tmp/nvim-treesitter execute 'set runtimepath^=' . fnameescape(stdpath('data') . '/site') runtime plugin/nvim-treesitter.lua e repro.py lua vim.treesitter.start(0, 'python') ``` Then run: ```sh nvim --clean -S repro.vim ``` ### Expected behavior Nvim should remain responsive when opening this Python file with Tree-sitter enabled. ### Nvim version (nvim -v) NVIM v0.13.0-dev-902+g7325e3b55a ### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same? no ### Operating system/version Ubuntu 26.04 ### Terminal name/version gnome-terminal ### $TERM environment variable xterm-256color ### Installation build from repo

comment_data.body:
Thank you for the thorough bug report - I was able to replicate.

Indeed, the match limit was removed. However, the kernel of the problem is related to a python treesitter query. Neovim does not handle treesitter queries for now anymore (nvim-treesitter is archived).

Consider disabling python injections (`vim.treesitter.query.set('python', 'injections', '')`) or using one of many treesitter parser managers that have popped up recently.

I have written a fix, though :thinking:

```diff
diff --git a/runtime/queries/python/injections.scm b/runtime/queries/python/injections.scm
index 2a120d9b..11607a3e 100644
--- a/runtime/queries/python/injections.scm
+++ b/runtime/queries/python/injections.scm
@@ -3,7 +3,12 @@
     object: (identifier) @_re)
   arguments: (argument_list
     (string
-      (string_content) @injection.content))
+      (string_start)
+      [
+        (string_content) @injection.content
+        (interpolation)
+      ]+
+      (string_end)))
   (#eq? @_re "re")
   (#set! injection.language "regex"))
                                                                                           
@@ -12,11 +17,14 @@
     object: (identifier) @_re)
   arguments: (argument_list
     (concatenated_string
-      [
-        (string
-          (string_content) @injection.content)
-        (comment)
-      ]+))
+      ((string
+         (string_start)
+         [
+           (string_content) @injection.content
+           (interpolation)
+         ]+
+         (string_end))
+       (comment)?)+))
   (#eq? @_re "re")
   (#set! injection.language "regex"))
```

Apply it by replacing/appending this to `~/.config/nvim/queries/python/injections.scm`:

```schema
(call
  function: (attribute
    object: (identifier) @_re)
  arguments: (argument_list
    (string
      (string_start)
      [
        (string_content) @injection.content
        (interpolation)
      ]+
      (string_end)))
  (#eq? @_re "re")
  (#set! injection.language "regex"))

(call
  function: (attribute
    object: (identifier) @_re)
  arguments: (argument_list
    (concatenated_string
      ((string
         (string_start)
         [
           (string_content) @injection.content
           (interpolation)
         ]+
         (string_end))
       (comment)?)+))
  (#eq? @_re "re")
  (#set! injection.language "regex"))

((binary_operator
  left: (string
    (string_content) @injection.content)
  operator: "%")
  (#set! injection.language "printf"))

((comment) @injection.content
  (#set! injection.language "comment"))
```

This topic has been discussed ad nauseum. Please browse existing discussions/issues or I suggest you look on reddit for another vendored parser manager.

> Neovim does not handle treesitter queries for now anymore (nvim-treesitter is archived).

This is a confusing statement. I guess you mean that we don't "maintain" downstream forks of treesitter queries? But we never did. nvim-treesitter was always a third-party project.

title: Python Tree-sitter becomes extremely slow on repeated f-strings
